domain.certificate.sentence.pending: The node will obtain one the first time somebody asks for this hostname over HTTPS. That needs DNS pointing here and port 443 reachable.
domain.certificate.sentence.issued: Visitors get HTTPS. The node renews it well before it lapses, without asking.
domain.certificate.sentence.renewing: The current certificate is still being served while the node obtains its replacement.
domain.certificate.sentence.failed: No certificate is in force, so HTTPS to this hostname will not complete.
domain.certificate.sentence.revoked: This certificate was withdrawn and is not being served.
domain.headline.notPlaced: Nothing is running this service yet, so there is no address to point this hostname at.
domain.headline.failedDefault: This hostname does not resolve to this service’s node.
domain.headline.pendingDefault: wisper is waiting for DNS to point here. It rechecks on its own.
domain.headline.noTls: Verified and served over plain HTTP. No certificate is being obtained for it.
domain.headline.noCertYet: Verified. The node obtains a certificate the first time somebody asks for it over HTTPS.
domain.headline.certFailedDefault: The node could not obtain a certificate for this hostname.
domain.headline.certExpired: This certificate has expired and HTTPS to this hostname will not complete.

domain.headline.certExpiresSoon.one: This certificate expires in {count} day and has not renewed yet.
domain.headline.certExpiresSoon.other: This certificate expires in {count} days and has not renewed yet.

domain.headline.serving: Verified, served over HTTPS, and the node is answering for it.
domain.headline.notServingYet: Verified. The node has not reported serving it yet.
domain.card.httpRedirectPending: · the HTTP redirect stays off until this hostname is verified
domain.confirm.remove.title: Remove {hostname}?
domain.confirm.remove.body: The node stops answering for it and its certificate is dropped. A hostname is unique across the whole platform, so once this row is gone anybody may add the same name to their own service - remove the DNS record too if you are done with it.
domain.page.title: Domains · {service}
domain.page.description.primary: This service answers at {hostname}. Any other hostname you add points at the same thing.
domain.page.description.none: No hostname points at this service yet. Add one and wisper will verify it and obtain a certificate for it.
domain.page.unplacedNotice: No node is holding this service, so there is no address for DNS to point at and nothing is being served. Hostnames added now are kept and checked as soon as the service is placed - deploy it, or start it from its overview, and this page will fill in the records to create.
domain.page.attention.allSingle: This hostname is not working yet.
domain.page.attention.allMultiple: None of these {count} hostnames is working yet.
domain.page.attention.eachBelow: Each one below says which record is missing.
domain.page.empty.title: No hostnames yet
domain.page.empty.description: Every hostname pointed at this service will be listed here with its verification state, the DNS record it still needs, and what the node last said about its certificate. Add one above to start.
domain.page.quota.title: Hostnames on this plan
domain.page.quota.description: Counted across every service in the organization. A hostname is unique across the whole platform, so removing one here releases the name for anybody to claim.
domain.page.readOnly: You have read access to this organization, so adding, verifying and removing hostnames are off. Everything on this page is still readable.
domain.form.title: Add a hostname
domain.form.description: Any name you control can point at this service. wisper checks DNS, then obtains a certificate for it.
domain.form.hostnameHint: Without a scheme and without a path. Wildcards are not accepted: a certificate for one needs a DNS challenge, and wisper does not manage DNS.
domain.form.tlsHint: Turn it off while the name still serves a live site elsewhere - the node will stop retrying a certificate it cannot get yet.
domain.form.targetPortHint: Only for a service listening on more than one port. Leave it empty otherwise.
domain.form.redirectToHint: Serve a permanent redirect instead of the service. This is how www.example.com sends visitors to example.com.
domain.form.forceHttpsHint: Only takes effect once the hostname is verified. Redirecting to a port whose handshake cannot succeed turns “not set up yet” into “broken”.
domain.form.readOnly: You have read access to this organization, so hostnames cannot be added from here.
domain.form.limitReached: This organization is using all {limit} of the hostnames its plan allows. Remove one, or ask an operator to raise the limit.
domain.cert.tlsOff: TLS is switched off for this hostname, so no certificate is obtained and visitors are served over plain HTTP. That is the right setting while DNS still points somewhere else - it stops the node retrying ACME against a name it cannot answer for.
domain.cert.noneYet: No certificate yet. The node obtains one the first time a visitor asks for {hostname} over HTTPS, which needs DNS pointing at it and port 443 reachable from the internet. Nothing on this page has to be pressed for that to happen.
domain.cert.liveBadge: This is what visitors are being served.
domain.cert.failedOnce: The last attempt to obtain a certificate failed.

domain.cert.failedTimes.one: Renewal has failed {count} time in a row. The count goes back to zero as soon as one succeeds, so this is happening now.
domain.cert.failedTimes.other: Renewal has failed {count} times in a row. The count goes back to zero as soon as one succeeds, so this is happening now.

domain.dns.verifiedSuffix: . wisper does not re-check a verified hostname, so moving DNS during a migration will not switch HTTPS off underneath a working site.
domain.dns.unplacedNotice: No node is holding this service yet, so there is no address to point {hostname} at. That is not something you can fix from here - deploy the service, or ask an operator whether the platform has room. wisper starts checking on its own as soon as it is placed.
domain.dns.record.pointHere.title: Point the hostname here
domain.dns.record.pointHere.note: The usual way, and the one that also makes the site reachable.
domain.dns.record.txtChallenge.title: Or prove ownership without moving traffic
domain.dns.record.txtChallenge.note: For a hostname still serving a live site elsewhere. wisper also accepts this record one level up, at the parent name, for DNS panels that will not create it here.
domain.dns.propagationNotice: Some DNS panels want the name relative to the zone rather than in full - in that case enter only the part before your registered domain, or @ for the domain itself. Changes can take a few minutes to propagate; wisper rechecks on its own and the button above forces one now.
domain.dns.notCheckedYet: Nothing has been checked yet. wisper looks this hostname up shortly after it is added.
domain.dns.noConclusion: The last check reached no conclusion.
domain.dns.field.name: Name
